about: Provenance of every transform in cwplans, modelled on W3C PROV (prov:Activity used / generated). Checked and exported to pipeline.jsonld by tools/check-data-register.mjs. Edit by hand when a tool changes.
conventions: Paths are relative to cwplans. "file" = tracked in git; "local" = not committed (gitignored raw data, caches, excluded outputs, or files a tool takes as arguments); "source" = a key of data-register.json sources. A source entry with "access": "manual download" means the file was downloaded by hand before the run and the tool reads only the local copy. Read from the code on 2026-10-03. "area" is a key of "areas" (the sections of METHODS.md); "faults" are F-numbers of the fault register in skills/docklands-data-curation/SKILL.md; "judgement" says where a hand decision enters and where it is recorded. "manual_activities" are methods that are not tools (hand curation, research catalogues, licence decisions); "gap" says what of a method is not committed as code.

activities.command: NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 KML_DOM_DIR=<dir with @xmldom/xmldom and linkedom> node cwplans/tools/find-kml.mjs <copy [id ...]|probe|all>
activities.method: Answers the owner's question 'Can you find any kml resources for the area?' (2026-10-05). A hand list of candidates, found by searching the project's own catalogues (London Datastore resources with format kml/kmz, the raw data.gov.uk walk: 4,499 of 59,451 datasets have a KML resource) and the open-data hubs of TfL, Walk Wheel Cycle Trust and Canal & River Trust, is fetched as the 3D page would fetch it (Origin header of the Pages site) and read with the page's own reader docklands/kml.js (a DOMParser from @xmldom/xmldom, description HTML through linkedom). For each: HTTP status, https, the CORS header, the counts of placemarks in the zone and in the model box, unsupported elements. Open layers that cannot be opened by URL (no KML, or a whole-London file) are written as zone-clipped KML with the page's writer into cwplans/feeds/kml/, with the source, licence and attribution in the Document description. Result: feeds/kml/catalogue.json and README.md.
rules: Politeness: one request at a time, at least 1.1 s apart, robots.txt read per host with walk-portals.mjs allowed() and obeyed, the project User-Agent.

Licence class as walk-portals.mjs licenceClass; only ogl, cc-by, odc-by and public-domain layers are copied or offered as examples; share-alike (except OSM content inside an open layer, marked odbl and osm derived), restricted and no-licence resources are listed with the reason.
cors yes = HTTP 200 over https and Access-Control-Allow-Origin * or https://danbri.github.io; a ?kml= link is made only for a file the reader parsed with at least one placemark in the zone.

Zone = the model box plus the Royal Docks and the Thames Barrier, WGS84 -0.095, 51.47, 0.08, 51.53; copies keep features that meet the box (polygons whole, lines cut at the box edge with one vertex beyond), the names and a few fields.
The copies are pushed to danbri/londat before the probe, which then reads them from raw.githubusercontent.com; the headless page test of every ?kml= link is stored in the catalogue as page_test.
activities.judgement: The candidate list, the fields kept in each copy and the colours are chosen by hand in the tool; the reasons for each listed (not usable) resource are in the tool and in feeds/kml/README.md.

activities.method: Fetches public permits, works, closures, planned events and markets for the Docklands zone (the 3D model box plus the Royal Docks margin) from TfL, DfT Street Manager, The Gazette, Tower Hamlets, the Planning London Datahub and OSM, and harvests venue and council event programmes from the event feeds in feeds/events.json; writes one dated snapshot per source ({meta, items}) and works.json, every item in one normalised shape, for feeds/whatson.html.
rules: Zone: "model" = WGS84 -0.095, 51.474 to 0.015, 51.522 (BOX_WGS84 of fetch-docklands.mjs; the tool prints the BNG box from docklands/data/area.js meta.extent: E 532400-539900, N 176700-182300); "east" = 0.015, 51.495 to 0.085, 51.522 (Royal Docks, ExCeL, City Airport). Items outside both are dropped and counted.

TfL lines: a status is kept when an affected stop lies in the zone; TfL sends lat/lon 0, so stops are placed through NaPTAN (stop-area id 940G/910G/930G -> station entry 9400/9100/9300, else by station name); a status naming no stops is kept only for a line that serves the zone (line-wide). Validity periods kept; start = first from, end = last to.

TfL buses: route disruptions grouped by identical text; kept when the text names a stop that lies in the zone on one of its routes, else when its opening "STREET, DISTRICT:" is a district wholly in the zone (E1, E1W, E14, E16, EC3*, SE8, SE10, SE16); a borough name alone does not place a diversion. Stop closures placed by the NaPTAN position of their ATCO code, grouped by text and dates.
TfL roads: disruptions active in the 90-day window whose TfL point lies in the zone; closed street segments of the same disruption id attached (at most 12).

Street Manager: unzip -p of the monthly archive split on }{"event_reference": (record count must equal the zip file count); BNG prefilter on the first coordinate, then OSTN15 to WGS84 and the zone test; the latest event per permit or activity reference. Permits kept when not cancelled, refused, revoked or closed and the end (actual, else proposed) is on or after the fetch date. Activities: skips and scaffolding counted, not kept; cancelled and ended dropped.

Gazette: robots.txt Crawl-delay 10 s between requests; only data.json searches and /notice/{id} pages (data.jsonld/.ttl/.rdf/.xml and ?view=linked-data are disallowed). The search geo point is the publisher office, so a notice is kept by issuing authority (zone councils, or Transport for London naming a zone borough). TTRO = text says temporary, section 14, 16A or experimental. Dates = day-month-year phrases on or after publication. Submitter (f:name, f:familyName) and signatory names dropped.

Tower Hamlets licences: the weekly table; premises-name column dropped (it sometimes holds a private licence holder name); placed at the postcode centre (postcodes.io, ONSPD). One week per snapshot; history is the git history of the snapshot.

Planning London Datahub: description has "temporary" and an event word (event, marquee, festival, stage, market, fair, funfair, ice rink, pop-up, filming, concert, exhibition); centroid in the zone; applications validated more than two years before the fetch dropped; description cut to 220 characters; facts and link only (GLA terms not confirmed as OGL).

Markets: OSM amenity=marketplace in the zone from the local extract (ways at the mean of their nodes); Tower Hamlets markets page parsed for name, days, place and times and joined by name, else placed on the OSM street it names.

Venue events: the feeds are read from feeds/events.json at run time (category ical, rss-atom, rest-api or whats-on-page; verified; a feed URL; ics, rss, atom or json; id, name or subject about events or what is on; not news, press releases, consultations, meetings, warnings, closures, works or notices; harvest: true/false on an entry overrides), so feeds added there join automatically. Kept per event: title (cut to 160), dates, venue, position, link; no description text. Date from the feed event fields (ICS DTSTART, RSS ev:startdate, WordPress ACF dates), a date in the title or link, or the Atom published day where checked by hand (Royal Docks, midnight entries only); events from today to 180 days ahead; undated items only from single-venue programmes. Position: postcode in the item, else the venue of the feed host (VENUES table, through its postcode). The Royal Docks feed mixes articles with events: only /whats-on/ links.
Gazette office postcodes (SE18 6HQ, SE6 4RU, E16 2QU, SE1 2QH, SE1 8NJ, SE1P 5LX, EC2V 7HH, EC2P 2EJ, E1 0HJ, E1 1BJ) are removed before postcode districts are read.

Network: User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1; one request at a time per host, at least 1 s apart (10 s for www.thegazette.co.uk); up to 5 tries with Retry-After or a doubling pause on 429, 5xx, timeouts and resets. Raw responses in data/raw/works/ (gitignored); NaPTAN, Street Manager archives and Gazette notice pages reused unless --refresh; --no-fetch rebuilds from the raw files.
activities.judgement: Zone margins, the rail lines treated as serving the zone, the postcode districts treated as wholly in the zone, the event words of the planning query and the dropped fields (premises names, submitter names, skips and scaffolding) are choices recorded in skills/cwplans-permits-and-works/SKILL.md and feeds/works/README.md.

activities.method: Builds the corridor model (Canada Water): a 10 m terrain grid, building footprints with heights, water levels, railways with tunnel chains and open cuts, roads, and stations and Wikidata places, in local metres around E0 535400, N0 179400.
rules: Terrain: median of the DTM in a 7 x 7 m window every 10 m.

Building height: OSM height tag; else the 90th percentile of DSM - DTM inside the footprint (at least 6 cells, at least 2 m) unless it is under half of building:levels x 3 m; else building:levels x 3 m + 1 m ('newer' when LiDAR exists); else the LiDAR value; else 6 m (0 for building=construction).
Buildings: centroid inside the box with a 2 m margin; single-outer multipolygons only.
Water: natural=water, waterway=dock or landuse=basin over 50 m2; level = 25th percentile of the DTM inside.
Tunnel portals: tunnel nodes shared with an open railway way, at the open track level (DSM on bridges, DTM otherwise).
Open cut: a tunnel point where the DTM is more than 6 m below the ground 25-35 m around; each run of cut points takes its lowest bed.
Published levels from data/sourced-levels.json are applied to the nearest tunnel point within 150 m (lib.mjs applyControls); superseded controls are skipped.

Scope branch, confidence low: the node's postcode is another E14/E20 postcode (a sibling branch is possible).
Scope chain: a chain branch's general page with no address on the node (chain-wide facts, not branch facts). Scope organisation: the same for a non-chain entity's own site.
Nodes with an address or position elsewhere are not attributed and are counted.

activities.method: Builds the Canary Wharf building registry: one record per OSM building outline with a stable cwb- id, its parts, occupants (OSM, FSA, Wikidata, chain-store branches, the Canary Wharf Group directory, the regulatory and public registers), owners, postcodes, Wikidata facts, and company and property joins.
rules: A building is an OSM building outline (way or multipolygon) whose vertex mean is in the Canary Wharf box; building:part shapes are listed under the outline that contains their centre.
Ids: reused from registry/ids.json by OSM element; new outlines get the next number in reading order (north to south in 100 m bands, then west to east); a retired id is never reused.

OSM occupants: named features with a shop, food and drink, office, amenity, leisure, tourism, healthcare, craft or transport role, placed in the outline that contains them or the nearest outline within 12 m; artworks, information boards, viewpoints and attractions are features, not occupants. Each OSM occupant keeps its tags opening_hours, cuisine, wheelchair, check_date, start_date, opening_date, operator, url, level, brand, brand:wikidata, website (or contact:website), phone (or contact:phone), email (or contact:email) and the other contact:* links (as contact).
FSA premises with a position in the box are placed the same way; the others are listed under their postcode when its tier is cw-*.

Wikidata: an OSM wikidata tag wins; else the one building-like item whose coordinate is in the outline (within 5 m) and no other building-like item is inside it; an item already named by an OSM tag is not attached to a second outline; other items inside are occupants 'located here'.
The Wikidata label replaces the OSM name; the OSM name is kept as osm_name.
Owners: Wikidata P127. Occupants also from P466 and from organisations whose P159 is the building.
UPRN points inside the outline (no tolerance) give UPRN counts, TOIDs and USRNs; LBSM2 homes are summed over the building's TOIDs.
Home figures are given only where at least 5 homes are counted (K = 5); otherwise 'fewer than 5'.
INSPIRE polygons that contain the building's centre are linked by INSPIRE id.

Companies and price-paid sales join a building when the postcode is one of its postcodes and the normalised address contains one of its keys (address, name, OSM name, Wikidata street address), and exactly one building matches.
A residential building lists only the count of registered companies, not their names.
Branches enrich the occupant with the same OSM or FSA id, else are placed by position (marked approximate when the position is a mall or postcode centre).
Buildings keep the OSM addr:housename (housename): it names the complex for a mall outline (Canada Place on 16-19 Canada Square).

CWG directory: an entry already linked by the branch join keeps that link. Else it joins existing occupants (OSM, FSA, Wikidata, branches, and CWG occupants added earlier in the same pass) when a name key is equal (registry/sources/brands/tools/cwg-fields.mjs nameKeys) and the place agrees, tried in this order: same mall (or same street or square), a shared postcode, or the building the entry itself would be placed in. Two different named malls never join (Canada Place and the One Canada Square mall count as one). An occupant with a CWG link takes a second entry only from another CWG section (cwg_also). Records of one source in two buildings: ambiguous, not joined.

CWG entries that join nothing become occupants (source cwg, role directory: <section>) placed by: the one building whose address key equals the street line (confidence high with the postcode, medium without); else the host outline of a named mall (the one outline whose OSM name, else addr:housename, is the mall name or starts with it; medium); else the one registry building with the entry postcode, or the one of them OSM tags as retail (low). Estate-wide entries, car parks and entries with no page, address or single building stay unplaced with a reason (cwg_unplaced, summary.joins.cwg).

Registers (registry/sources/registers/): records are excluded when the address is not a place: GIAS correspondence addresses (address_role), the registered-office service at E14 5HU / 10th floor 5 Churchill Place, care-of and accountant addresses. Keys in order: UPRN (OS Open UPRN point inside an outline; not used when one register gives the UPRN to records at two or more postcodes, or when the UPRN point is over 150 m from the register point), the register point (inside or within 12 m; an FSA point within 3 m of its postcode centre is a postcode, F7), a named mall in the address (the mall host outline, F4; the point outline kept as point_in), street address with the postcode, street address alone when one building matches a numbered address key, the name of an occupant at the same postcode or mall, the postcode alone when one registry building has it, the ONSPD centre is within 50 m of it and the address names no other street (never for a charity). A charity placed by address in a residential building (homes or a residential building tag) is left unplaced. A record whose name matches an occupant of the chosen building enriches it; else it is a new occupant (source = register, role register: <name> or head office (ODS) for ODS organisation records, current false for closed or inactive records). Each link (occupant.registers[]) keeps register, id, kind, status, key, precision, confidence; source ids are copied to the occupant (urn, ods_code, cqc_location_id, charity_number, company_number, ofsted_urn, gambling_premises_id, active_places_site_id, fhrs_id). Unplaced records and rejected UPRNs are listed (registers_unplaced, registers_uprn_rejected).

activities.method: Fetches the star catalogue, the constellation lines, satellite orbital elements, hourly weather and tide-gauge readings for the Sky panel of the 3D page (docklands/sky.js) and writes small JSON snapshots; the weather and tide files cover the London date given and the next day (the owner's photo evening, 3 October 2026).
rules: Stars: Bright Star Catalogue rows with a J2000 position and V <= 5.5 (2,887); columns from the CDS ReadMe: HR 1-4, RA 76-83, Dec 84-90, Vmag 103-107, B-V 110-114; RA and Dec to 0.001 degree, V and B-V to 0.01; a missing B-V becomes 0.6; sorted by V.

Constellation lines: every line string kept; longitude turned into RA 0-360 degrees; coordinates rounded to 0.01 degree. The Milky Way outlines of the same repository are not fetched (no stated licence); the page computes the band from galactic coordinates.

Satellites: the three requests merged, one record per NORAD catalogue number; OMM fields kept as published. CelesTrak keeps no history, so a snapshot holds the elements current at fetch time (run within a day or two of the date). One request per group per run (CelesTrak: at most one download per 2 hours).
Weather: the forecast API's past hours (best_match model, UK Met Office UKV first for London; it has visibility, which the ERA5 archive lacks); values as published, hourly, London time.

Tide: 15-minute instantaneous readings in m AOD, UTC times, sorted; no gap filling; EA gives readings only, no predictions. The page (sky.js cleanGauges) leaves out a reading whose difference from the nearest other gauge departs more than 0.45 m from the median of that difference over 2 h either side (fault F21), then interpolates linearly by chainage along data/river.json between the gauges. The EA has no tidal gauge between Tower Pier and Charlton (station search of 2026-10-04, 15 km round the estate).

Star names: rows of IAU-CSN whose designation is an HR number present in stars.json (324 of 451 names); columns found by the positions of the header titles (Name/Diacritics, Designation, Con), because names can hold spaces; the diacritic form is kept.

Clouds: the EUMETSAT cloud mask PNG kept as sent. The page (sky.js) reads white pixels (R, G, B > 200) as cloud, takes the mean over 60 km round the box centre, and raises each layer's Open-Meteo cover by 0.9 x (local mask - mean), clamped to 0..1, so the mask places the cloud and Open-Meteo keeps the amount; the mask moves with 2.2 x the 10 m wind for up to 90 minutes from its slot. Other times only with Fetch ticked (EUMETView sends CORS headers; the mask appears about 25 minutes after the slot; none before 2020-09-01). Parallax (about 1.6 km north for cloud at 1 km over London) is not corrected.

London City Airport: the landing thresholds are the two ends of the main runway way (ref 09/27; its displaced-threshold ways are left out); the page draws each approach as the extended centreline rising at 5.5 degrees (the published glide path) from 15 m over the threshold (50 ft assumed) out to 12 km. No live aircraft: OpenSky (written licence for any live product), adsb.fi (personal non-commercial), ADS-B Exchange (commercial), adsb.lol (ODbL share-alike) and airplanes.live (terms behind a bot challenge) were checked on 2026-10-04.

Messier: all 109 rows of the HEASARC table (M 102 is not in it); RA and Dec from sexagesimal J2000 to degrees (0.001); size = the larger dimension in arcmin; the notes column title-cased as the common name. OpenNGC was not used (CC BY-SA).
Network: User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1; three retries 3, 6 and 9 s apart on timeouts and 5xx (the agent proxy drops connections now and then); 4xx is not retried; files overwritten on every run.
activities.judgement: Source choice and licence decisions (BSC5 as public domain, d3-celestial lines as BSD-3, CelesTrak with no stated licence and flagged for review, Vieira Milky Way outlines refused) are recorded in data-register.json sources and docklands/README.md "Sky, time, weather and tide".

activities.method: Walks the London Datastore (a DataPress site with a CKAN-compatible API): reads the whole catalogue from the v3 export, writes it compact (one dataset per line); triages every dataset by written rules (licence class, relevance to the zone, kind, whether the project already holds or lists it, value themes, join keys, sensitivity, score); harvests the shortlisted open datasets and keeps the features that meet the 3D model box, as GeoJSON in WGS84 with a meta member (source, URLs, fetch date, licence, attribution, method, counts).
rules: Catalogue: publisher = organisation (logo title), else CKAN maintainer, else custom.author; geo = custom.geo (spatial granularity); update_frequency = custom.update_frequency; resource format = file extension; resource URL = https://data.london.gov.uk/download/{dataset}/{id}/{file}. Not kept: descriptions, contact names and emails, logos.

Licence class: OGL v2/v3 -> ogl; Creative Commons Attribution -> cc-by; ODC Attribution -> odc-by; Public Domain, PDDL -> public-domain (these four are open); CC BY-SA and ODbL -> share-alike (never harvested, CLAUDE.md); CC Non-Commercial and All Rights Reserved -> restricted; TfL Transport Data Service Licence -> other; empty -> none (never harvested).

Relevance, first match: zone-place (title or tag names a place in the 3D model box; "upon Thames", "Thames Estuary", "Thames Gateway", "Thamesmead" removed first); zone-borough (names only Tower Hamlets, Southwark, Lewisham, Greenwich, Newham, City of London); other-area (names 1-3 places, none in the zone); london-fine (geo finer than a borough, or with no geo a ward/LSOA/MSOA/OA/postcode/UPRN/TOID word or a spatial format); london-borough; london-coarse; unknown.

Have: a dataset id or slug in a committed file of cwplans: data-register.json, pipeline.json, tools, data files -> held; a .md note, feeds catalogues, the 2026-10-03 survey -> listed; an "excluded" list or a survey "left out" line -> excluded-before; else new. feeds/london-datastore/ and the generated docs are not read.

Sensitive (catalogued, score 0, never harvested): title names homicide, victims, strip or intimate searches, suicide, custody, stop and search, hate crime, domestic abuse, sexual offences, safeguarding, missing persons, rough sleeping (CHAIN), bariatric incidents.

Score = relevance weight (zone-place 5, zone-borough 4, london-fine 3, london-borough 1.5, unknown 1, london-coarse 0.3, other-area 0) x max(theme value, 0.5) x recency (newest resource year >= 2024: 1, >= 2021: 0.8, >= 2016: 0.5, else 0.3) x (machine-readable format ? 1 : 0.4) x (a join key finer than a borough ? 1.3 : 1) x (open ? 1 : 0) x (held 0, listed 0.8, new 1).

Harvest zone: a feature is kept when its geometry meets the 3D model box (BNG E 532400-539900, N 176700-182300): a vertex inside, an edge crossing (Liang-Barsky) or the box centre inside a polygon. Whole geometries kept, not cut; whole_in_zone and in_cw (meets the Canary Wharf registry box -0.03, 51.498, -0.005, 51.51) are added.

Coordinates: GeoPackage SRS 27700, or a custom definition on Airy 1830 with the BNG projection (srs_id 100000) -> BNG; output WGS84 to 6 decimal places through OSTN15. CSV points: a row is WGS84 when |x| <= 180 and |y| <= 90, else BNG; empty or zero coordinates -> no_geometry.

Dropped fields: names matching e-mail, phone, contact, fax, mobile, owner name, person (none matched in the 13 harvested files). uprn_suspect: a UPRN field with an exponent or 9+ digits ending in 5+ zeros (F22). The Brownfield Register is read from its CSV, not the GPKG (F23).

Network: one request at a time over the whole tool, at least 1.1 s apart; up to 6 tries with Retry-After or a doubling pause on 429, 5xx and network errors; User-Agent glitchcan-cwplans/0.1. robots.txt disallows only /debug, /manage/, /login, /logout.

Details walk (--details, 2026-10-04, all 1,305 datasets): /api/v3/dataset/<id> adds per resource the publisher's generic format (kind) and an md5 hash, and per dataset the description; the catalogue keeps a details member (resource count, kinds, archivedAt, nextReviewDate, geo, the granularity words and zone place names found in the description, resources only in the details record). The description text itself is not kept. Result: 0 archived, 0 resources missing from the export, geo identical to the export for all 1,305.

Zone references (refs): a code is a zone code when a live or terminated ONSPD (August 2026) postcode whose grid reference lies in the 3D model box carries it, or when its polygon in the Datastore's Statistical GIS Boundary Files (20od9: LSOA/MSOA 2021, OA/LSOA/MSOA/wards 2011, wards 2014 and 2018) meets the box. Zone UPRNs: OS Open UPRN X/Y in the box; zone TOIDs: the LIDS TopographicArea TOIDs of those UPRNs (raw cache only).

Area from the data (probe): every open, not sensitive dataset whose metadata relevance is unknown, london-borough or london-coarse (671) is opened: up to 3 readable resources (finer-area file names first, then csv/txt/json/xml, sheets, gpkg, zip; newest first; stop at the first zone signal). Caps: text formats the first 1 MB (HTTP Range); xlsx/xlsm/xls/ods whole up to 20 MB (SheetJS, 3,000 rows and 40 sheets read); zip whole up to 60 MB (shapefile record envelopes and dbf, inner csv/sheets/gpkg, 12 entries, zone borough and place names first); GeoPackage whole up to 100 MB (every geometry envelope). Documents (pdf, docx, images, audio) are not opened.

Area class from the data, first match: D1 zone-point (a row's lat/lon or easting/northing, or a feature envelope, in or meeting the box; the value decides WGS84 or BNG); D2 zone-uprn (a zone UPRN in a UPRN column) or zone-postcode (3+ distinct zone postcodes; the postcode's letters must be one of the 121 UK areas); D3 zone-code (an OA/LSOA/MSOA/ward code in zone-codes.json); D4 zone-place (2+ distinct zone place names, 3+ cells); D5 london-fine (5+ London coordinates, small-area codes, 20+ postcodes, UPRN or TOID columns, no zone value in the sample); D6 borough-rows (zone borough code or name, nothing finer); D7 london-coarse (London, region, national, or other boroughs only); D8 none. The data class replaces the metadata relevance of a probed dataset.

Final state, first match (every dataset gets one): F1 sensitive; F2 harvested (held); F3 not-open (licence); F3b deferred (excluded before by the project); F4 links only (unavailable when every link failed the Datastore QA check, else deferred); F5 unavailable (every probe request failed); F6 listed-for-harvest (relevant with a machine-readable resource; reason and size); F7 deferred (relevant, documents only); F8 not-relevant (data: borough rows, London or coarser, none); F9 not-relevant (metadata names only places outside the zone); F10 deferred (data not readable: size cap, format, no readable resource); F11 deferred (not probed).

Old ward codes (refs-old-wards, 2026-10-04): the 2003 CAS and 2005 statistical ward codes (00BGGG form, ONSPD wdcas03cd and wdstl05cd) of the postcodes in the box, one ONSPD query with distinct values; and the 2011 Census merged wards (E36) of the zone 2011 wards from the ONS lookup WD11_CMWD11_LAD11_EW_LU. Without them 2001- and 2011-Census ward tables read as having no zone rows.
activities.judgement: The harvest shortlist (the HARVEST table in the tool) was chosen by hand from the ranked triage: open, relevant, new, machine-readable, not geometry-only where an alternative exists; the choices and the ranked backlog with reasons are in feeds/london-datastore/README.md. The probe rules (caps, thresholds of D2 and D4, the place list) were set by reading the first full run: one cell naming Deptford or one publisher postcode (City Hall) made a zone dataset of a payments list, so D2 needs 3 distinct zone postcodes and D4 2 names in 3 cells; census table ids (QS101EW) read as postcodes until the UK postcode area list was added. Fatal fires (24yo6, incident postcodes) was added to the sensitive titles by hand.

activities.method: Harvests the London Datastore datasets that triage.json lists for harvest, by written rules instead of a hand table: picks the readable resources (one per file stem, best format, size caps, hand rules where the general rules would take too much or the wrong file), reads every row and feature (CSV streamed, large xlsx streamed with ExcelJS, xls/ods with SheetJS, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, shapefiles, zips entry by entry), keeps the zone rows (zone codes, postcodes and sectors in profiled columns, UPRNs, TOIDs, coordinates) and the features that meet the 3D model box, and records the outcome of every dataset in harvest-log.json; triage then states no-zone-rows datasets not relevant (F8b) and unreadable ones deferred (F10b).
rules: formats: readable resource formats: gpkg, geojson, zip, csv, tsv, xlsx, xlsm, xls, ods; json and txt only when nothing else is readable. Documents, images, kml/kmz, rds and other binary formats are not read.

dedupe: one resource per file stem (file name lower-cased, separators to "-", without the extension and without trailing format words shp, gpkg, geojson, csv, xlsx, xls, gis, data, and the layout words long, wide; a wide file is taken before its long twin): gpkg > geojson > zip > csv > tsv > xlsx > xlsm > xls > ods > json > txt, then the newest; identical md5 = one resource.

caps: a resource over 1,200 MB is not read (disk); a dataset with more than 40 stems or 2,500 MB in total takes the newest 12 stems unless a hand rule (HAND) says otherwise. Raw files over 20 MB are deleted after reading.

names: datasets about town centres or stations (metadata geo Town Centres or Train Stations, or the title) also match names: a cell equal, after normalising (case, &, punctuation, words such as station, DLR, town centre), to the name of a zone town centre (town-centres harvest, polygon meets the box) or a zone station (TfL StopPoint, NaPTAN metro and rail stations in the box); keys town-centre:<name>, station:<name>; weaker than a code.

zone_row: a table row is a zone row when a cell is a zone OA/LSOA/MSOA/ward code (zone-codes.json, any vintage), a zone postcode (ONSPD grid reference in the 3D model box), a zone postcode sector (the sector of a zone postcode, in a sector column) , a zone UPRN in a UPRN column (OS Open UPRN in the box), a zone TOID in a TOID column, or its own coordinates lie in the box (lat/lon or easting/northing columns, judged by value). Ward tables: the City of London row (E09000001) is a zone row (the City is one ward-level unit there). The first matching key is recorded per row (zone_keys).

transposed: a sheet whose area codes run across a row (3 or more codes in one of the first 15 rows, and no code in a column to the left below it) is read column-wise: the label columns and the columns of zone codes are kept, every row; zone_keys then name the columns ("column ward:E05009323").
header: sheets: the up to 4 rows above the first data row (a row with an area code, a postcode or a coordinate) are header_rows; CSV: the first line.

geometry: features (GeoPackage, GeoJSON, shapefile) are kept when they meet the box (walk-london-datastore.mjs harvestGeo); a table whose single header row names coordinate columns becomes points in the .geojson (the row cells are the properties).
numbers: numeric cells are kept as numbers; non-integers rounded to 6 significant digits (file size); identifiers (leading zero, E0.. codes, osgb TOIDs) stay text.
personal: columns whose name matches e-?mail|phone|tel(ephone)?$|^tel|contact|^fax|mobile|website_contact|^owner_?name|person are dropped (contact details), also under the cwplans exception.

outcome: harvested: at least one zone row or feature; no-zone-rows: every row or feature read, none in the zone (then triage states the dataset not-relevant, rule F8b, with the counts as evidence); not-readable: no resource could be read (deferred, F10b); documents-only: the zips hold documents only (deferred, F7); deferred-by-hand: a HAND rule with the reason (deferred, F3c); held-for-owner: not run (owner decision pending; the state is left as it was).

clip: a polygon of over 1,000 vertices that reaches beyond the zone (a London-wide boundary) is cut to the 3D model box plus 500 m (Sutherland-Hodgman, ring by ring) and marked clipped_to_zone; smaller geometries are kept whole.
as_table: a hand rule may keep rows with coordinates as a table (the LAEI grid summaries are one row per cell, source and year: 33,540 points made 15 MB of GeoJSON for LAEI 2010).
thin: a hand rule may thin a regular 20 m grid (LAEI concentrations) to 1 cell in 5 each way (a 100 m grid), by the BNG cell index of the point or of the cell centre; the meta says so.

activities.method: Copies a spreadsheet-sourced file and amends only the UPRN cells that a spreadsheet rounded (F22). Every cell is classified (rounded: scientific notation, or 9+ digits ending in 5+ zeros; catalogued only: empty, text, decimal, out of range, padded, duplicate across venues, not in OS Open UPRN, over 150 m from its OS Open UPRN point, and per-layer constant position offsets, F25). Each rounded venue is recovered by the first route that gives exactly one candidate inside the range the rounded value allows: (a) the same dataset in other formats, layers and releases, (b) OS Open UPRN points in the venue's OSM building outline, (c) registers with UPRNs; else (d) unknown with the reason. Writes the amended copy beside the source and an amendments file with one entry per changed cell, every unknown, the catalogue, the rules and the measured precision of routes a and b (each valid 12-digit UPRN rounded to 3 and 6 digits and recovered blind).
rules: The source file is read, never written; a value that is not in a rounded class is never changed.

Range: Excel rounds to k significant digits; the true value lies within half a unit of the last kept digit (1.00023E+11 -> [100022500000, 100023500000); plain 200000000000 -> k = non-zero prefix -> [150000000000, 250000000000)); rounded forms of the same venue in other releases narrow it by intersection.
Venue: rows with the same normalised name within 50 m are one venue; candidates are pooled and every row gets the same answer.
Route a: same normalised name (or one contains the other, 8+ characters) and point within 50 m (or the same address1 without a point); exactly one distinct full UPRN in range.

Route b: the smallest OSM building outline containing the venue point (none: OS Open UPRN points within 10 m); in a layer with a measured constant offset the moved point is tried too; exactly one OS Open UPRN point in range.
Route c: as route a over GIAS, ODS and Active Places rows with UPRNs.

Confidence: high = route a, exact name, OS Open UPRN point of the candidate within 150 m of the venue (or of the venue moved by its layer offset); medium = other route a, route c, route b with the candidate within 1 m of the venue's own point in an outline of at most 25 UPRN points; low = other route b. High and medium applied; low recorded, not applied.
Two or more candidates: never chosen between; the venue stays unknown with the candidates listed.
activities.judgement: The thresholds (50 m, 150 m, 10 m, 1 m, 25 UPRN points) and the confidence levels are hand choices, recorded in the tool header constants and in skills/cwplans-london-datastore/SKILL.md "Amending rounded UPRNs"; the measured precision that supports them is in the amendments file meta.validation. The 2025 Cultural Infrastructure Map (2rj5o, no licence on the Datastore) was left out by decision.

activities.method: Checks the 3D page's shaders for what a phone GPU would do differently from the headless SwiftShader renderer: opens the page in headless Chromium, captures every compiled shader source, and counts each program's uniform rows, varyings, samplers and attributes against the WebGL 1 minimums; then re-runs the shaders' risky maths (hashes, time arguments, far positions, derivatives) in Node with every intermediate rounded to IEEE binary16, beside fp32.
rules: fp16: round to nearest, ties to even, 10-bit mantissa, exponents -14 to 15 with subnormals, overflow to infinity (Node 22 has no Math.f16round).

A case fails only for a shader declared mediump (on a phone mediump may be fp16); cases for shaders that ask for highp where present (HIP, PRE) are reported as notes, because every OpenGL ES 3 GPU has highp in fragment shaders.
Each case quotes the shader text it mirrors; when that text is gone from the page the case is reported STALE and the tool fails.

Uniform rows are counted without packing (every float, vec2 and vec3 a whole row), so a real count is at most the one shown; minimums: 128 vertex and 16 fragment uniform vectors, 8 varyings, 8 texture units, 8 attributes.
Writes nothing; exit 1 on a failing or stale case.

activities.method: Opens the 3D page with the Line drawing style in headless Chromium at four views and sizes, renders the line drawing and makes the Plotter SVG of the same camera, draws the SVG at the canvas size in the plotter's own page frame and matches the ink pixel by pixel; prints the edge counts, buffer bytes, build time, edges drawn, frame time and recall and precision within 1 and 2 px.
rules: Ink: luma under 0.8 in the line drawing; the SVG's strokes drawn black at one canvas pixel, the credit left out.
Recall: plot ink with line-drawing ink within the tolerance (a square of 2 x tol + 1 px); precision: the other way.
Fails on a page error, a style that did not switch on, or recall under 95% or precision under 97% at 2 px.
Frame times come from SwiftShader (the GPU in software): not a phone. Writes images only with --out.

activities.method: Joins the tree inventories, OSM trees and the Trees Outside Woodland lone-tree crowns into one list of trees in model metres, with OS Open Greenspace sites, OSM green areas and TOW canopy groups as green rings.
rules: Box: BNG E 532400-539900, N 176700-182300 (fetch-docklands.mjs BOX_BNG); WGS84 to BNG through OSTN15; x = E - 537550, z = -(N - 180300); every value rounded to 0.5 m.

Ethics (CLAUDE.md, Data ethics): a tree keeps only position, taxon (scientific and common name), height, crown spread, source and record id. Notes, sponsorship, memorial, dedication, inscription, address, owner and maintainer fields are never read into the payload; each source lists its dropped fields in sources[].dropped.

Tree precedence: GLA public realm inventory first; then TPO points (planning.data), OSM natural=tree nodes and TOW Lone Tree crowns, each added only if no tree already kept lies within 3 m (TOW: within the crown radius, at least 3 m).
GLA class values ("05 to 10 m") become the middle of the class; "Not recorded" is null. Species "Unknown Tree Species" and common name "Plant" give no species.
TPO: records with an end date are left out; the taxon is read only from Tower Hamlets names of the form "Common (Scientific)"; Southwark names (site descriptions, URLs) are dropped.
OSM: species, else taxon, else genus (with the :en names); height under 60 m and diameter_crown under 40 m kept.
TOW Lone Tree: centroid of the polygon, height = maxht, crown = diameter of a circle with the polygon area (tow_area_m). Group of Trees, Small Woodland and NFI OHC polygons become greens with meanht.

Greens are clipped to the box (Sutherland-Hodgman) and simplified (Douglas-Peucker 0.5 m; TOW 1.5 m, its outlines follow the 1 m LiDAR grid); OSM multipolygon inner rings and shapefile holes are kept as holes.
Network for the source files: see fetch-trees.

activities.method: Solves a daytime photo's camera and capture time: a pinhole camera fitted to tower tops of the model, shadows on a level deck back-projected through it, and the sun azimuth matched to a time with astronomy-engine. Prints JSON; the results are copied by hand into the photo folder's README and the docklands-sky skill.
rules: Camera: heading (from grid north), tilt, roll and focal length by Nelder-Mead least squares on the landmark pixels; principal point fixed at the image centre; landmark = the apex (pyramid) or the centroid of the top tier at its top height in docklands/data/towers.json; a landmark with a null y is fitted in x only.

Shadow: the pixel of a post foot and of the shadow of its cap are back-projected to the plane 1.5 m below the eye; sun grid azimuth = bearing foot->shadow + 180 degrees; true azimuth = grid + grid_to_true_deg (1.54 here). The azimuth does not depend on the assumed camera height; the printed shadow lengths do (given for 1.3, 1.5, 1.7 m).

Time: astronomy-engine Equator(of date, aberration) + Horizon(refraction "normal") for the observer in the points file; bisection on the azimuth between 06:00 and 18:00 UTC of the date. Result = the time of the mean azimuth; range = the times of the smallest and largest azimuth.
The library is run in a vm context; times are passed as that realm's Date (its instanceof check fails on a Date of the main realm).

The 3D page view ?view=greenlandday uses the same four landmarks refitted with roll 0 (the page camera has no roll): heading 51.9, tilt 6.45, field 99.9, rms 2.7 px (fitted by a grid search in the session, numbers in the docklands-3d-page skill).
activities.judgement: The pixel positions in points.json are read by eye from 2x and 4x enlargements (which point is the foot of a post is a judgement: the base plate hides it); recorded in points.json and the README.

activities.method: Solves the camera of any photo of the zone, ground or air: a pinhole camera with eye position, heading, pitch, roll, focal length and optional radial distortion k1, fitted by Levenberg-Marquardt (numeric Jacobian) to landmark pixels (tower tops, named places, given coordinates), shoreline pixels (distance to the projected OSM water outline) and horizon pixels (the sea-level dip from the eye height). Reports rms, formal 1-sigma per parameter from the covariance, per-point residuals and hold-out residuals. Library tools/view-mcp/view-lib.mjs, also served as the docklands-view MCP (tools/view-mcp/server.mjs).
rules: Model metres: x = E - 537550, z = -(N - 180300), y = m OD; WGS84 by the page's own quadratic fit (meta.geo) and its Newton inverse.
Tower landmark = the apex (towers.json top.apex) or the centroid of the top tier at its top height; place landmark = area.js places at its ground height.
Earth curvature is applied to every point (drop d^2/2R with refraction k = 0.13); the horizon target is the sea-level dip -sqrt(2h/R') with weight 0.5 (the visible horizon is hills 20 to 40 km away).
Hold-out points are projected but not fitted; the run restarts once from its own result.
The page view takes the fitted camera without k1 (the page has no lens distortion): eyeView(eye, heading, pitch, hfov) plus roll.
activities.judgement: Pixel positions and which photo feature is which landmark are read by eye from grid enlargements; recorded in points.json and the photo folder's README (with the failed hold-out).

activities.method: Builds the index of works in progress: PLD records grouped into sites, a status per site from the LDD commencement and completion dates and the decision, and joins by position to NOTAM cranes, Street Manager highway activities, OSM construction areas, the brownfield register, site allocations and Wikidata, each with a confidence; hand-written facts (developer pages, the owner's photos) joined by planning reference.
rules: Zone: model box WGS84 -0.095, 51.474 to 0.015, 51.522 plus the east margin 0.015 to 0.085, 51.495 to 51.522 (as fetch-works.mjs); the PLD centroid decides.

Grouping (union-find): same reference base (suffixes /A1, /S, /NC, /P1 ... removed), a description or relied-on permission that cites another record's reference within 300 m, or centroids within 10 m.

Status per group: S1 LDD commencement within 7 years, no completion (high); S1b status Commenced without a date, decided within 7 years (medium); S2 commenced more than 7 years ago, never completed (low, F32); S2b S2 with an overlapping OSM construction area, a NOTAM crane within 60 m or a Street Manager crane, hoarding or compound within 50 m -> on site (medium); S3 completion within 2 years and not before the latest commencement (high); S4 approved within 5 years, not lapsed (lapsed_date in the past) or superseded, no commencement (medium); S4b S4 with a NOTAM crane within 60 m or an overlapping OSM building=construction -> on site (medium, F33); S5 undecided application or appeal (high). Completed more than 2 years ago, refused, withdrawn, lapsed: counted, not listed. A commenced record is never dropped for a past lapsed_date (F33).

Footprint: PLD wgs84_polygon of 50 m2 or more (smaller = point marker, F35); else the smallest overlapping OSM building=construction outline, else landuse=construction; else a circle of the stated site area; else 25 m round the centroid. footprint.from says which.

Matches: M1 NOTAM crane to the nearest on-site, approved or stale site within 150 m (high within 60 m); M2 Street Manager activity within 120 m (high within 50 m); M3 OSM construction feature within 30 m (high when overlapping); M4 brownfield point within 40 m (geox/geoy WGS84 or BNG per row, F23); M5 site centre in a site allocation polygon; M6 Wikidata item within 40 m (high within 15 m with a shared label word, medium with the word, low without).

Kept per source: ids as published (PLD id and lpa_app_no, NOTAM id, Street Manager activity id and USRN, OSM type/id, brownfield site reference, allocation OBJECTID, QID), dates, and the snapshot or fetch date. PLD descriptions cut to 300 characters; no NOTAM text; OSM tags limited to name, landuse, building, construction, dates, operator, developer, levels, height, description, website, ref, address.

Heights: PLD building_details max_height as entered (m AOD where the description says so); storeys max of the lead record's buildings, else of the group; developer and CTBUH figures only in approved.web from facts.json.
Output: one site per line; borough names without "London Borough of".
activities.judgement: The status windows (7, 5 and 2 years), the "major" filter and the match distances are judgements, recorded in the tool header, meta.status_rules and meta.match_rules and the cwplans-construction skill. facts.json is hand-written from crawled pages and the owner's photos (crawl list inside it).

rules: Politeness: one request at a time over the run, at least 1.1 s apart, robots.txt read for every host before the first request and obeyed (longest matching rule), backoff on 429 and 5xx with Retry-After, the project User-Agent.

Licence class (licenceClass in walk-portals.mjs): OGL, CC BY, ODC-By, CC0/PDDL/public domain are open; NC or closed is restricted; CC BY-SA and ODbL are share-alike (never harvested; OSM is the only share-alike exception); 'no conditions apply' alone is open-unclear; no licence is none (metadata only). data.gov.uk records with no licence whose resources all sit on GOV.UK, ONS, Nomis, NHS Digital, DfT road traffic or data.police.uk count as ogl-site-terms (those sites' terms give OGL v3.0).

data.gov.uk scope: S1 local publishers (zone boroughs, LTGDC, Canal & River Trust, TfL, Royal Museums Greenwich, PLA, local NHS), S2 named national publishers, S3 the GLA (the London Datastore: state walked-elsewhere), S4 other publishers whose title or tags name a zone place or borough; out of scope only counted per organisation.

data.gov.uk states, first match: T0 by hand; T1 sensitive title; T2 held (dataset id, or a name of 15+ characters with a hyphen, in a tool, data-register.json or pipeline.json); T3 walked-elsewhere (GLA); T4 unavailable (no resources); T5 not-relevant administrative (payments, spending, staff, contracts, FOI); T6 not-open; T7 not-relevant other area (bounding box misses the zone, or the title names another region, county, city or London borough); T8 deferred documents only; T9 listed-for-harvest (zone place, zone borough, London-fine or national-fine); T10 not-relevant coarser than a borough; T11 deferred area unknown.

Zone place names (title and tags only, not the description): the London Datastore list plus Thames Barrier, Tideway, Lower Lea, Leamouth; not when the text has tree or crop words (Poplar is also a tree: 'Energy Crops Scheme' and short rotation coppice records matched it).

planning.data.gov.uk: zone = entities whose geometry intersects the box polygon (the platform's spatial query); for documents, agreements and plans the entities of the zone planning organisations (GLA 144, Greenwich 150, Lewisham 198, City 203, Newham 246, Southwark 329, Tower Hamlets 350). States P0 by hand (held from another source), P1 harvested, P2 ended, P3 not-open, P4 empty, P5 code list, P6 nothing in the zone, P7 listed-for-harvest, P8 deferred.

Harvest: whole geometries that meet the box are kept, rounded to 6 decimals, with in_zone, whole_in_zone, in_cw; EA flood zones are simplified (0.5 m) and cut at the box (clipped_to_zone). Fields matching e-mail, phone, contact, owner name, person, officer, agent, applicant are dropped and listed.

Committed outputs stay small: the data.gov.uk triage lists datasets one by one only for the states that need a decision or hold data; the bulk states are name lists keyed by state, rule and reason. National files stay raw and uncommitted; only zone extracts are committed.

Borough portals: City of London map service layers with the box envelope count; licence per layer from the City's data.gov.uk INSPIRE record (F42); layers about people or their sites deferred (B2); Southwark and Greenwich observatories read from the Esri UK InstantAtlas master tables and metadata service (indicators of national publishers are walked-elsewhere, B3); Lewisham licence from each JKAN source file; states B0-B8.

ONS Open Geography: ArcGIS search catalogue; states G1-G8 by product family from the title; lookups read by code list in batches of 60.

activities.method: Runs a subset of the existing fetch tools as child processes with their own politeness (fetch-live.mjs bikes lifts crowding ukpn overflows notams; fetch-river.mjs levels river-bus; fetch-ais.mjs --listen=0), asks two small endpoints itself (TfL line status by mode, Open-Meteo current weather; one request each), reads the snapshot JSON the tools wrote, replays this month's run files (cache/runs/) into a working SQLite (node:sqlite, WITHOUT ROWID tables with primary keys on the source's fetch or reading time), inserts the new snapshots and writes only the rows that were new as one small gzip JSON run file. The first run of a new month replays the previous month's run files into cache/live-YYYY-MM.sqlite (VACUUM) and removes them. Then writes cache/latest.json: per theme the newest fetch in compact columns and a 24 h series. --no-fetch appends from the snapshots already in the checkout. Planned to run hourly from a GitHub Actions workflow in danbri/londat (skill cwplans-londat-cache).
rules: Idempotent: every table has a primary key with the fetch time of the snapshot (meta.fetched) or the reading time (tide, AIS positions, weather); INSERT OR IGNORE, so a second run on the same snapshots adds no rows.

Politeness is the fetch tools' own (one request at a time per host, >= 1.5 s for TfL, >= 1 s for EA, >= 2 s and no stream for Open Waters); the tool adds two requests per run with up to two retries 3 and 6 s apart.
Facts only, as the snapshots: no NOTAM text, no customer letter text from UK Power Networks, no JamCam images.
Small private craft are never listed: the AIS filter of fetch-ais.mjs is repeated (ITU type 36/37, class B without a type are dropped) and their count is kept in ais_fetches.private_counted.
Places (docks, stations, overflows, piers, gauges) are stored once in places and updated in place; state rows hold only ids and numbers.
A run goes into the month of its newest snapshot; tide readings within 48 h of a month boundary can appear in two month files.
Git size (coordinator, 2026-10-05): no binary file is committed per run; each run adds one run file (measured size in the skill) and latest.json; the monthly SQLite is committed once.

manual_activities.what: Source catalogue for the underground estate
manual_activities.method: Four research agents searched for plans, levels and 3D models of the malls, stations and tunnels; each entry was fetched directly or as an Internet Archive copy and its licence read; sources not used are listed with the reason. The README tables are generated from the JSON files.
rules: Nothing is copied into the model except cited level values (data/sourced-levels.json).
Copyright plans (Canary Wharf Group, TfL, Crossrail) are for reference by eye, not for copying.
Each exclusion records why (licence, no levels, duplicate, unreachable).
manual_activities.gap: The generator of feeds/underground/README.md is not committed.

manual_activities.what: Catalogue of live feeds, APIs and event sources
manual_activities.method: Research agents surveyed data sources in seven areas (341 added on 2026-10-03, 135 left out with reasons) and event, calendar, news and openings sources (124); each URL was fetched from the container and its status, CORS, licence and a sample recorded; check-feeds.mjs and check-events.mjs re-check them.
rules: Only official, published or openly licensed sources, and only cameras their owners publish for public viewing.
Left out with the reason: directories of unsecured private cameras, people-search and face-recognition sites, personal licence registers that list named individuals.
A source behind a bot challenge is "not verified", never "verified" (F11).
manual_activities.gap: The generators of feeds/README.md and feeds/EVENTS.md are not committed ("generated and by hand").
decisions_recorded_in: feeds/feeds.json and feeds/events.json (status, licence, excluded section)

manual_activities.what: Hand decisions on FSA and CWG brand matches
manual_activities.method: Matches that the rules cannot decide (an NSI prefix variant, an alternate name, a business type that does not fit the brand) are judged by hand, one record at a time, and written to decision files that the tools read on every run.
rules: A decision names the record, the brand item and accept or reject, with a reason.
Undecided and rejected matches are listed apart by the tools, never joined.

manual_activities.method: For branches whose OSM website is missing or a bare home page, the branch page was found by hand on the brand's own locator and its URL recorded; storelocator.mjs then checks it like any other.
rules: A URL on the brand's own domain; the UK site first.
Only the URL is recorded, not page content.

manual_activities.what: Open-licence subset of the museum and heritage records
manual_activities.method: Cuts records-open.json from records.json (fetch_records.py): records under CC0 (Wikidata), OGL (Historic England, OGL-licensed ADS records) or CC BY (Portable Antiquities Scheme), without the "sensitive" flag (burial or memorial context).
rules: Records flagged sensitive (44: burials, cemeteries, graves, memorials, skeletons) are left out (CLAUDE.md, Data ethics).
Records under other or unstated licences are left out.

manual_activities.what: Open photos, facade regions and footprint widths for the facade measures
manual_activities.by: facade agent, then the main session
manual_activities.method: Searched Wikimedia Commons and Flickr for photos of the Canary Wharf towers, downloaded only CC0, Public Domain Mark and CC BY images, recorded author, licence, page and the face shown; chose a facade region in each photo by eye; computed oriented bounding boxes of the OSM footprints for face widths.
rules: CC BY-SA, NC, ND and all-rights-reserved images are not downloaded; seven CC BY-SA Commons photos were looked at for facts only.
The face shown is judged from landmarks when a photo has no geotag (32 of 45 Flickr photos).
Commons and Flickr rate-limit the container (429, retry after 600 s): wait, do not hammer.
decisions_recorded_in: registry/sources/facades/photos.json (face and how it was judged)

manual_activities.what: Pixel-art palette and music list for the 3D page
manual_activities.method: The pixel-art palette: 24 colours extracted from an owner-supplied reference picture by PIL median cut and k-means (a one-off run; the picture is not stored), plus 9 accent colours added by hand. The music list: tracks chosen by hand from Wikimedia Commons with title, artist, licence and page.
rules: Pixel-art colours do not follow height alone (owner, 2026-10-03: it reads as a heat map); materials carry the variety.
Music: CC BY 3.0 tracks (Kevin MacLeod) served by Wikimedia Commons with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the page can analyse them; the credit is shown while a track plays.
manual_activities.gap: The palette extraction was a one-off script and is not committed.

manual_activities.what: Licence check of every source before commit
manual_activities.by: hand (each session), owner decides open cases
manual_activities.method: Before a source is fetched into a committed file, its licence is read on the provider's own page and recorded in data-register.json sources (name, licence, attribution, note). Restricted, proprietary and share-alike sources other than OSM are not committed; open questions wait for the owner.
rules: Not committed: the VOA rating list (restricted licence), the PLA ArcGIS layers (no licence stated), the Canal & River Trust layers (no commercial use).
Not used: GLA canopy and green cover 2024 (all rights reserved), Curio Canopy (CC BY-SA), Wikipedia text (CC BY-SA), CC BY-SA Commons photos (looked at only).
Held for the owner: the Crossrail long section (licence not stated).
Needs an account, not fetched: HM Land Registry CCOD and OCOD, EPC data.
Re-check the Gambling Commission (no licence on the download page; data.gov.uk says OGL) before anything leaves prototyping.

manual_activities.what: Keeping pipeline.json and the register in step with the tools
manual_activities.method: Every new or changed tool updates its pipeline.json activity in the same commit (used, generated, method, rules, network, deterministic, after, area, faults, judgement); every new data file gets a data-register.json entry in the same commit; then check-data-register.mjs --write regenerates DATA-REGISTER.md, METHODS.md and pipeline.jsonld.
rules: The check fails on an unlisted tool, an empty method or rules, an unknown area or fault id, an unregistered data file, and a page that shows OSM data without the attribution link.
Source identifiers are kept as they come (OSM type/id, QID, UPRN, TOID, FHRS id, company number, cwb- id): they become IRIs.

manual_activities.what: Analysis of the error classes and the fault register
manual_activities.method: Reads the audit output, names the error class of each wrong value, writes the analysis and the proposed compositing layers, and records faults in our own joins and tools in the fault register with the measured effect of each fix.
rules: Catalogue first: name the class, add a check if none covers it; do not edit the record (owner, October 2026).
Change a tool only for a pipeline or join-rule fault; re-run the audit and compare the counts.

manual_activities.what: Crown lighting policy, campaigns and dated colour observations
manual_activities.method: Web searches for how the colour of One Canada Square's top is chosen, its lighting systems, campaigns and contractors; each fact written in our own words with its URL, date and how it was read. Commons thumbnails and the owner's photos of 3 October 2026 looked at by eye: what is lit (pyramid faces, halo band, facade wash, nothing) and its colour; an approximate hex from the mean of the brightest 20% of pixels in the lit area (30% for dim pyramids).
rules: No text or image copied: facts only from all-rights-reserved pages and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA); CC BY-SA photos give URL, capture date and the colour seen.
A campaign needs a press, council, partner or designer source with a date; an observation needs a dated photo, post or report of the night itself.
A colour seen with no campaign source stays an observation with the reason unknown (3 October 2026); gaps between dates are never filled.
The apex aviation light (white, flashing) is never a campaign colour.
Confidence low when the pyramid is small, dim or in cloud; EXIF capture time is the photographer's local clock.
manual_activities.gap: The pixel measurements were run from the session scratchpad (a 10-line Pillow script: crop, sort by brightness, mean of the top fraction); the boxes are in no committed file.
